chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn Hamza, from his grandfather, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say at the end of his sermon: 'Blessed is he who has good character, pure nature, sound inner self, and beautiful outward appearance; who spends his surplus wealth, restrains his surplus speech, and is fair to people with himself.'

key_terms.أنْصَفَ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: He was fair to people with himself (treating others as he treats himself)
key_terms.سَرِيرَتُهُ: His inner self or secret deeds
key_terms.طُوبَى: Blessedness or happiness, often referring to a tree or state in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What are the key moral characteristics of the Prophet's sermon according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on justice, this hadith from Abu Hamza al-Thumali encapsulates the Prophet’s (SAW) comprehensive ethical framework, linking inner purity (sirrah) with outward integrity ('alaniyyah). It underscores the Shia emphasis on self-accountability (muhasabah) through three practical disciplines: charitable expenditure, restraint in speech, and equitable self-regard. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the integration of spiritual character (akhlaq) with social justice in Islamic practice.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Hamza, from his grandfather, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said at the end of his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Toba’ (a Blessed tree in Paradise) is for the one who makes good his manners, and cleans up his temper, and corrects his secretive deeds, and improves his unconcealed deeds, and spends the excess from his wealth, and withholds the excess from his words, and is fair with the people from himself’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Hassan ibn Hamza from his grand father from abu Hamza al-Thumali from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah at the end of his sermon would say, ‘Tuba (a tree in paradise) is for those whose moral behavior is polite, whose consciences are clean, whose privacy as well as public matters are all well, who give the excess in their properties in charity, who hold back their unnecessary words and yield to justice for people against their own souls.’”
